entries.title: I Corinthians 8:1
segments: ¶But concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know, (for we all have knowledge: knowledge puffs up, but love edifies.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:2
segments: If any one think he knows anything, he knows nothing yet as he ought to know [it].

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:3
segments: But if any one love God, *he* is known of him):

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:4
segments: ¶--concerning then the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol [is] nothing in [the] world, and that there [is] no other God save one.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:5
segments: For and if indeed there are [those] called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, (as there are gods many, and lords many,)

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:6
segments: yet to us [there is] one God, the Father, of whom all things, and *we* for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, by whom [are] all things, and *we* by him.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:7
segments: ¶But knowledge [is] not in all: but some, with conscience of the idol, until now eat as of a thing sacrificed to idols; and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:8
segments: But meat does not commend us to God; neither if we should not eat do we come short; nor if we should eat have we an advantage.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:9
segments: But see lest anywise this your right [to eat] itself be a stumbling-block to the weak.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:10
segments: For if any one see thee, who hast knowledge, sitting at table in an idol-house, shall not his conscience, he being weak, be emboldened to eat the things sacrificed to the idol?

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:11
segments: and the weak [one], the brother for whose sake Christ died, will perish through thy knowledge.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:12
segments: Now, thus sinning against the brethren, and wounding their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:13
segments: Wherefore if meat be a fall-trap to my brother, I will eat no flesh for ever, that I may not be a fall-trap to my brother.
